newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called down on stock data, weak ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called down on stock data, weak ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open sharply lower Thursday in continuance of the weakness on ACCESS, sources said.
January over-the-counter trading ranged from about $3.32 to $3.36 per million British thermal units early but then rose to the $3.36-3.41 range. Jan settled Wednesday at $3.493.

After the lower-than-expected storage data were released by the American Gas Association, indicating a drop of 72 bcf to 75 percent of capacity, January fell 15.3 cents to a low of $3.34 before last trading at $3.355.
Before the release of the data, most traders were anticipating a drawdown of about 84-92 bcf, with some expectations as high as 115 bcf.

Stocks were still 214 bcf, or eight percent, below year-ago, but most expected the gap to narrow significantly in coming weeks, as declines fail to match last December's weekly average drawdown of 142 bcf.
Traders said support in January was first at $3.19, then $3.11 and $3.04. Resistance was seen in the low-$3.50s and then at $3.70.
In Wednesday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices firmed 20 cents to about $3.40. Midcontinent prices gained about 15 cents to the mid-$3.30s but were still about 30 cents under December indices.

Temperatures are expected to remain near or slightly above-normal Friday throughout most of the U.S. In the National Weather Service's six- to 10-day outlook, temperatures are forecast to be mostly normal to above-normal in the East but below-normal throughout the remainder of the U.S.
